items.title: Perfectly Replicating Red Bull...Then Making It Caffeine-FREE
items.description: Red Bull (and basically all energy drink brands for that matter) refuses to make a caffeine-free version of their iconic drink...so I reverse engineered the recipe with the help of mass spectrometry! Want to help support LabCoatz? Of course you do! Feel free to donate, become a channel member, or join my Patreon using the links below! https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCcT_WBynr2K8nANsVrR8BYw/join https://www.patreon.com/labcoatz https://www.paypal.com/paypalme/labcoatz Want a sample for your own testing? Check out these fine eBay links to my pages! If possible, try to limit your purchase quantity to two (2) per order, as the boxes I have won't hold more than that many: Regular (caffeinated): https://www.ebay.com/itm/318922197439 Caffeine-free: https://www.ebay.com/itm/318922194180 A massive thanks to Ben from @MassSpecEverything and Vince from @Neptunium for their mass spectrometry work! It's truly what made this video possible! I'd also like to thank everyone who help with the tasting, including my good friend and storm chaser @MesoHunterWX! An additional shoutout to @Artofdrink, who has one of the best (and only!) videos about making an authentic energy drink: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_sYBfkpQBiQ CURRENT RECIPE: no changes so far! I'd honestly leave out the C-14 aldehyde and phenethyl alcohol though... Red Bull syrup (mix one part with four parts carbonated water): 490g sucrose (regular sugar) 50g glucose (powder, not syrup) 35g citric acid 7.65g sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) 2g magnesium carbonate 20g taurine 1.6g caffeine 0.39g niacinamide (vit. B3) 0.1g pyridoxine HCl (vit. B6) 0.1g calcium pantothenate (vit. B5) 1mL cyanocobalamin (vit. B12) solution (0.1g/L) 500mL riboflavin solution (saturated) 0.6mL Durkee caramel color 10mL flavor solution (see below!) Once mixed, top off to a volume of 1 liter using water Red Bull flavor solution: 35.2g ethyl butyrate 8.85g vanillin 4.25g ethyl vanillin 2.1g ethyl isovalerate 1.7g methyl cinnamate 1.85g ethyl maltol 2.85g isoamyl acetate 0.3g a-ionone (b-ionone will work) 2.95g diethyl succinate 1.65g propyl cinnamate 0.3g allyl caproate 0.2g ethyl caproate 0.7g benzyl acetate 0.85g isoamyl butyrate 0.6g ethyl acetate 0.13g orange oil (optional) 0.1g isoamyl isovalerate (optional) 0.1g y-undecalactone (optional) 0.1g dimethyl anthranilate (optional) 0.1g phenethyl alcohol (optional) Dilute these flavors to a volume of 1 liter using food-grade propylene glycol or alcohol WARNING: this project deals with a weak acid (citric acid) and potentially toxic substances, namely caffeine. Make sure you thoroughly understand what you're doing before attempting anything seen in this video! 0:00 Intro 1:51 The basics 9:19 Deciphering the flavor 11:33 Synthesizing flavor esters 13:44 Synthesizing alpha-ionone 17:49 Initial testing 18:33 Missing flavors (thanks Mike!) 21:26 How to make Red Bull 23:34 Preparing the flavor 30:33 Mixing up the syrup 31:36 Red Bull at last! 32:08 Taste tests 34:37 Caffeine-free Red Bull 38:15 Minimalist Red Bull 39:46 Flavor for sale! Check my eBay! 40:52 Looking forward

items.description: Taurine is found in a lot of energy drinks, and since I'm working on replicating Red Bull, I figured I'd show how it's made on a laboratory scale! Want to help support LabCoatz? Of course you do! Feel free to donate, become a channel member, or join my Patreon using the links below! https://www.youtube.com/@LabCoatz_Science/membership https://www.patreon.com/LabCoatz https://www.paypal.com/paypalme/labcoatz Go check out my storm chasing channel @labcoatz_chases! Want a high quality lab coat? Check out‪‪‪‪ @geniuslabgear and my affiliate link (this is basically as close as I can get to offering regular channel merch): https://geniuslabgear.com/LABCOATZ Hydrobromic acid syntheses: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OC7iBvqStFc https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8gADsHx7CnA https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4ei_xUIhRas WARNING: making taurine is more expensive than simply buying it, and it's potentially hazardous. Hydrobromic and hydrochloric acids are corrosive, some of the organic byproducts may be toxic, and sodium sulfite can release toxic sulfur dioxide gas when acidified. If you attempt anything shown in this video, you do so at your own risk, and it is recommended that you wear protection and work in a well-ventilated area. 0:00 Intro: taurine is a thing 1:05 Ingredients 1:33 Synthesis: 2-bromoethylamine HBr 4:21 Synthesis: taurine from 2-bromoethylamine HBr 5:12 Purification 6:27 Recrystallization 7:43 Final yield 8:10 Looking forward (and back)

items.title: Perfectly Replicating Coca Cola (It Took Me A Year)
items.description: The Coca Cola secret formula is one of the best kept secrets in recent history...and I hate secrets. So, naturally, I deciphered it with the help of mass spectrometry and created a chemically-identical replica! Want to help support LabCoatz? Of course you do! Feel free to donate, become a channel member, or join my Patreon using the links below! https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCcT_WBynr2K8nANsVrR8BYw/join https://www.patreon.com/labcoatz https://www.paypal.com/paypalme/labcoatz A massive thanks to Vince from @Neptunium and Ben from @MassSpecEverything, their mass spectrometry work is truly what made this video possible! Check out their videos here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V45lSJJ-d-M https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JYN5sNOiA6s An additional shoutout to @GlenAndFriendsCooking and @HowToCookThat, who put out excellent videos on making cola, and especially to @Artofdrink, who has several highly educational beverage-related videos, as well as one of the best colas I've tasted! https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KWaNiwcQK2M https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_VG-gvzr-8g https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o2yLvseG5UM Finally, thanks to @Nighthawkinlight for demonstrating orthogonal (Taguchi) arrays in his video! Be sure to check out these other videos from people who tried (or at least brought attention to) the recipe: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0usa0L5owbs https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rphwEzFe6Jo https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9f3ZO4N0RC8 CURRENT RECIPE: same as video, but use 10 grams of tannin, 150 grams of glycerin, and 43mL of 85% phosphoric acid. And if you use Durkee caramel color (since Shanks no longer seems to be available), use 185mL instead of 320mL, since it's much stronger. New warning regarding tea tree oil: this ingredient is not FDA-approved from what I can tell, and can be toxic in high doses, so use at your own risk. That said, it does appear to be GRAS, and the amounts used here are over 5X less than the maximum allowable (10 ppm). PER LITER OF SODA (VERSION 111C): 104 grams sugar (dissolved in a minimum volume of water) 1mL flavor solution A (alcohol-based) 10mL flavor solution B (water-based) Top off to 1 liter with cold carbonated water FLAVOR SOLUTION A: dilute 20mL of the following oil mixture to a volume of 1 liter using food-grade 95% alcohol. 45.8mL lemon oil 36.5mL lime oil 8mL tea tree oil (from Australian tea tree, Melaleuca Alternifolia) 4.5mL cassia cinnamon oil 2.7mL nutmeg oil 1.2mL orange oil (regular sweet orange) 0.7mL coriander oil 0.6mL fenchol (any version of alpha-fenchol should work) FLAVOR SOLUTION B: dilute the following mixture to a volume of 1 liter using water. 185mL Durkee caramel color 150 grams food-grade vegetable glycerin 43mL 85% phosphoric acid 10 grams wine tannin 9.65 grams caffeine 10mL 5% vinegar 10mL vanilla extract (or a solution containing 0.95 grams per liter of vanillin) If you like glass bottle "Mexican" Coke, just increase the lime in the final mix. I haven't actually made an effort to replicate glass bottle Coca Cola, but that seems to be basically the only difference. Here's the research paper I referenced throughout this project: https://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/jf504954p?ref=article_openPDF Regarding the types of essential oils to use, there is not a standard for "food grade" essential oils...as long as the sample is verifiably pure, that's as good as it gets. Brands like NOW and Aura Cacia seem to be reasonable. For the fenchol, different CAS numbers should be suitable as long as the sample is over 90% alpha-fenchol. There are no substitutes for fenchol, and despite what Wikipedia says, basil does not contain a significant amount of it...based on my research, it might have some fenchone or fenchyl acetate, but that's it, and these are minor components. Fenchol has a very distinct, heavily musty, earthy, or moldy smell, with some camphor or mint-like notes in high doses. WARNING: concentrated phosphoric acid is mildly corrosive and undiluted flavors and essential oils can be irritating or toxic. Never consume, unless properly mixed and diluted to safe levels. Tea tree oil is toxic in high doses (same for a lot of flavors, honestly), but the few microliters used in this cola are well within the limits for beverage use. You will honestly absorb less by drinking this soda than you would by using a tea tree lotion or mouth wash, and as the data shows, it's all chemically the same as Coke! 0:00 Secrets secrets secrets 1:18 A fool's errand...or not? 2:56 What's in Coke? 3:29 Coca (but not cola) 4:10 Flavor basics and early trials 7:17 Mass spectrometry (thanks Vince and Ben!) 9:12 Research papers and key discoveries 11:54 Spreadsheet time 12:20 The missing flavors 13:44 A year of testing 14:23 A BIG discovery...we nailed it 15:27 How to make Coca Cola 17:16 Mixture A: 7X flavor 18:47 Mixture B: water-based ingredients 19:46 Mixing up the cola 21:41 What do other people think? 23:27 Looking forward

items.title: 'Daily Dose Of Internet' Got It Wrong...Was This Salsa Poisoned?
items.description: A few weeks ago, @DailyDoseOfInternet shared a video...a video involving salsa that was "somehow producing electricity". There seemed to be a lot of confusion regarding what was causing the effect, so I decided to figure it out for myself! My theory (which I actually commented on the video): the salsa was mixed with aluminum phosphide, a common pest control poison that emits a self-igniting gas called phosphine...possibly in an attempt to unalive someone. But was I right? Only one way to find out! Wanna help support LabCoatz? Feel free to donate, become a channel member, or join my Patreon using the links below! https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCcT_WBynr2K8nANsVrR8BYw/join https://www.patreon.com/labcoatz https://www.paypal.com/paypalme/labcoatz Want a high quality lab coat? Check out ‪‪‪‪@geniuslabgear through my affiliate link (this is basically as close as I can currently get to offering regular channel merch): https://geniuslabgear.com/LABCOATZ Original Daily Dose video with the "electric salsa": https://youtu.be/VVbr1FOdVNE?t=129 The family salsa recipe (I guess it's technically a pico de gallo...kinda?): 4 large tomatoes 8 tomatillos 2 jalapeno peppers 1/2 white onion Cilantro (hard to say how much, we use a full bunch from Walmart, so maybe a cup or so? You could also leave it out if you're sensitive to the flavor) Garlic salt (to taste) Optional: one or two hot peppers (I used a few home-grown heatless Moruga scorpion peppers for the flavor) Ingredients are washed, blended to desired consistency, and strained of excess liquid. That's it, no cooking required! WARNING: don't replicate what you see in this video. Aluminum phosphide and phosphine are more toxic than cyanide, microwave oven transformers can easily electrocute you if mishandled, and self-igniting gases like silane and phosphine can cause serious fires. Every experiment was conducted under controlled conditions, and is being shown for educational purposes. 0:00 Something is bothering me... 0:47 Making salsa 1:20 Can salsa make electricity? 1:47 Does microwaving help? 2:25 Salsa vs welder 3:05 Salsa vs 2000-volt transformer 3:47 Sodium 4:40 Phosphine: was the salsa poisoned? 7:00 Silane 8:39 Final verdict
